grammar.explanation: Greek participles are verbal adjectives that must agree with their antecedent in gender, number, and case. They express relative time to the main verb and can function attributively (with article) or circumstantially (expressing when, why, how, etc.).
rules: Present participle = action simultaneous with main verb
Aorist participle = action prior to main verb
Circumstantial (no article): when, because, although, etc.

exercises.question: Translate: ταῦτα εἰπὼν ἀπῆλθεν.
exercises.answer: Having said these things, he departed. / After saying these things, he departed.

exercises.question: Explain: ὁ λέγων ταῦτα vs λέγων ταῦτα
exercises.answer: ὁ λέγων ταῦτα = 'the one saying these things' (attributive); λέγων ταῦτα = 'while saying these things' (circumstantial)

readingPassage.greek: Ὁ Ἰησοῦς ταῦτα εἰπὼν ἐξῆλθεν σὺν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ. Ἰδὼν τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος. Οἱ ἀκούοντες τοὺς λόγους αὐτοῦ ἐθαύμαζον.
readingPassage.translation: Jesus, having said these things, went out with his disciples. Seeing the crowds, he went up on the mountain. Those hearing his words were amazed.
